Action.description:
Every uncommon CLI operation, as one union both frontends produce.

An action carries no origin of its own: `action/execute` names the conversation it was submitted from, so a queued action cannot retarget itself to whatever page happens to be visible when it drains.

oneOf.description: Clear the conversation and start a new session (`/clear`, `/reset`, `/new`).
Clean expired session storage (`/gc`).
Compact the context. It follows the page it was submitted on rather than the page that is visible when it runs.
Write a starting chart and its agreement into the project (`/team new`).
Drop the crew's notes past their life (`/team memory gc`).
Send the foreground command to the background. Interrupting it is `turn/interrupt`, not an action.
A persisted theme preference. Which colours get painted is frontend-local; that the choice was saved is not.

originConversationId.description: The page the action was submitted on. It stays the action's origin even if the user switches pages before it drains.

disposition.description: The same dispositions a submission gets: an action asked for while a turn is busy queues like any other input.

ActionFamily.description: Which family an action belongs to, for grouping in a command menu.

ActionId.description: The stable identity of an action, shared by `action/list` metadata and the registry that dispatches it. Unlike every other identifier here it is a name rather than an epoch-scoped handle: a client may hard-code it.

ActionInfo.description: What `action/list` publishes for one action. The command menu and `/help` derive from the same registry that dispatches it.

preconditionScope.description: The revision a mutation of this action must carry, when it needs one.

unavailableReason.description: Why it is unavailable right now, when it is.

originConversationId.description: Availability is answered for this page; absent answers for main.

ActionResult.description: The outcome of a synchronously applied action. Views are not returned here — help, status, context, config, skills, tasks, and images are structured reads (`config/read`, `catalog/read`, `resource/read`), and each frontend renders its own.

message.description: One short English line worth showing. A projection, not a contract: clients branch on the status, never on this.

revision.description: The new revision of whatever the action mutated, for a client holding a precondition.

oneOf.description: Valid, and nothing changed (selecting the model already selected).

ActivationKind.description: How the client's response was activated. Only keyboard approval inside the guard is premature; denial, cancellation, and pointer approval are immediate.

oneOf.description: Neither — a programmatic client with no human activation to report.

AgentKind.description: A standing member of the project's crew, or someone hired for one task.

AgentResource.description: One agent instance. Each is its own session with its own engine, so the engine it runs on is reported rather than assumed to be the session's.

def.description: The definition it was spawned from, when it had one.

pending.description: Messages waiting in the inbox for this instance to claim.

prompt.description: The task this instance is working on, or last worked on. A roster's task line is drawn from it, and a client that had only the description would be showing what the instance *is* where it means to show what it is *doing*.

recentActivity.description: The tool lines this run has produced, oldest first and bounded. What a `Running` row says it is doing right now is the last of them; without it a client can only report that something is running.

unacked.description: Messages sent to it that nobody has answered yet.

oneOf.description: One of `choices`.

AssetOrigin.description: Where an asset's bytes live. Session assets are cleaned up with the session; transcript assets stay reconstructable from durable content.

data.description: Base64, bounded well below the server frame ceiling.

AssetRecord.description: A registered asset. Registration snapshots the bytes into server-owned storage; the caller's path is never borrowed or deleted afterwards.

AssetRegisterPathParams.description: Registration validates the file and snapshots its bytes into server-owned storage. The caller's path is never borrowed later and never deleted; a GUI holding clipboard bytes writes its own temporary file and may remove it once this succeeds.

BackgroundCommandResource.description: A command running outside the foreground slot. Watch state only: the protocol invents no cancel or re-foreground capability the CLI does not have.

oneOf.description: One round finished; a periodic command may run again.

CatalogKind.description: Which catalog a read asks for. Every one of them is answerable before a session exists: a GUI picks a provider and a model on the way in.

CatalogReadParams.description: Answerable before `session/start`: a GUI picks its provider and model on the way in, which is the job `--inspect` used to have.

provider.description: Which provider's models to list. Ignored by the other catalogs.

ClientCapabilities.description: What the client can do. A controlling client must be able to answer interactions; initialization fails otherwise rather than silently auto-denying a prompt that has not happened yet.

experimental.description: Experimental methods the client opts into by name.

Collection_for_AgentResource.description: A bounded slice of an otherwise unbounded collection: the revision it was read at, how many entries exist, and the ones worth carrying in a snapshot. The remainder is read through the paginated resource methods.

Collection_for_BackgroundCommandResource.description: A bounded slice of an otherwise unbounded collection: the revision it was read at, how many entries exist, and the ones worth carrying in a snapshot. The remainder is read through the paginated resource methods.

Collection_for_TaskResource.description: A bounded slice of an otherwise unbounded collection: the revision it was read at, how many entries exist, and the ones worth carrying in a snapshot. The remainder is read through the paginated resource methods.

CommandId.description: A background (promoted or detached) command run.

CommandTail.description: A foreground command's live tail: bounded lines after carriage-return handling and escape removal, plus how many lines have completed. It replaces the previous sample and never appends to final output.

ComposerMode.description: How the composer reads the text it was handed.

oneOf.description: The `!` prefix: the line is a shell command.

ConfigLayer.description: One settings layer that contributed to the effective configuration, so a frontend can show where a value came from without reading files itself.

ConfigSnapshot.description: The effective configuration. No credential values, only where they come from.

ContextUsage.description: Context window occupancy, with the point at which the core compacts on its own — the same three numbers the CLI's `/context` reads.

oneOf.description: The console: session actions, shell input, and the turn the user's prose starts. Rendered through the same projection as every other conversation.

ConversationMarkReadParams.description: Called only once content is actually visible. Prefetch and resynchronization cannot clear unread or mention state, because reading never does.

cursor.description: Absent starts at the tail. A cursor from a stale `historyGeneration` is refused rather than mixing pre- and post-rewrite history.

oneOf.description: An agent conversation whose instance was stopped; its history stays and a direct message revives it.
A room, which receives posts and never owns a turn.

ConversationSnapshot.description: An atomic read of one conversation. Reading never marks it read.

historyGeneration.description: The generation the item page was cut at; a continuation from a stale one is refused.

ConversationSummary.description: The bounded state of one conversation, including the attention state a frontend cannot safely infer from text.

historyGeneration.description: Bumped only by structural rewrites (rewind, compaction). Ordinary streaming and appends leave it alone, so an item cursor stays valid.

isMember.description: The user may speak here. False for a room they have not joined.

revision.description: Bumped by every change to this summary; carried by `markRead` so a stale client cannot clear attention it never saw.

CredentialSource.description: Where a credential came from. Presence, source, and status only — no key material reaches a snapshot or an event.

followUps.description: Follow-ups the runtime has chased with so far, and the bound on them.

private.description: The private lane rather than a room.

reason.description: Why a dropped message will never arrive.

DeliveryState.description: Where a direct message got to. A peer's turn prose does not settle this; only an observable message back does.

EpochId.description: One run of the server process. Every other identifier is scoped to it; a restart invalidates them all.

ErrorData.description: The structured half of an error. Human-readable text is English and sanitized; clients never branch on it.

ErrorScope.description: What the error is about, so a client knows what to re-read.

oneOf.description: The request itself was malformed or arrived out of order.

EventMeta.description:
The header every event carries.

`seq` is assigned when the actor mutates state, not when a transport serializes the event: it is strictly increasing and gapless within one server epoch. `ts` is stamped at the same instant. `caused_by` names the operation that asked for this, when one did.

coalescedFrom.description: Set only when a transport merged a run of adjacent append deltas for one item into this frame: the `seq` that run began at. Every event from `coalescedFrom` through `seq` is represented here, so a client checking for gaps still reads a gapless stream. The core never sets it — merging is the transport's, and this is how it stays honest about what it did.

Feedback.description: A warning, notice, or error raised outside any single turn. It carries a stable code so a frontend branches on the code, never on the text.

FeedbackId.description: One raised warning/notice, so it can be cleared by identity.

Interaction.description: A pending application request. It outlives the JSON-RPC call that announced it: a prompt recovered from a snapshot stays answerable.

remainingGuardMs.description: Milliseconds left on the confirmation guard, recomputed for every event and snapshot. Only keyboard approval is held back by it.

feedback.description: What the user wanted instead; it travels to the model through the permission-error path so a denial carries a direction.

oneOf.description: The user dismissed the prompt. Fails closed.

InteractionPrompt.description: What the server is asking. Exactly the decisions it advertises are valid.

sessionScope.description: Absent when no verified session rule exists; `allowSession` is then rejected rather than invented.

oneOf.description: An explicit destructive confirmation (session delete, rewind apply).

itemId.description: The ordered item the resolution committed, when it commits one.

Item.description:
Ordered semantic content. Not a terminal row and not a provider event.

An item belongs to a conversation and may carry a `turnId`; the input item that opens a turn carries none. `item/completed` is authoritative over every delta that preceded it.

oneOf.description: Prose the user submitted.
Prose the model produced.
A message that arrived from main or from a colleague. `to` is the private lane's target when it is not this conversation's own owner.
A room post. Completed on arrival, with no turn of its own.
Model reasoning, appended by `item/reasoningDelta`.

A tool call and its authoritative result. Whether it succeeded is the item's own `status` — a tool-specific status beside it would be a second answer to the same question, and two answers can disagree.

artifact.description: Output too large for the item; read through `asset/readChunk`.

input.description: The resolved input, exactly as the tool received it.

oneOf.description: A standalone shell run: the `!` command and its promoted background form.

background.description: The run was promoted to the background; it is watch state from here.

oneOf.description: History was summarized. The numbers are the compactor's own outcome.
History was cut back to an earlier point.
The user interrupted. `marker` is the exact string the transcript recorded, so the screen and the model read the same sentence.
Structured notice committed into the flow rather than raised as transient feedback.
A question the user answered. This one does enter the model's context.
A permission decision, for display and audit. Explicitly excluded from model input.
An image or other asset, by opaque reference. No terminal cell geometry travels with it.

ItemCursor.description: A cursor into one conversation's history. Bound to the generation it was issued under; a continuation from a stale one is refused rather than mixing pre- and post-rewrite history.

ObligationKind.description: Something the conversation is waiting on the user for, stated rather than inferred from prose.

oneOf.description: The user was mentioned and has not replied.
A question is open on the user.

ProtocolRange.description: The major the client speaks and the minor window it accepts.

QueueEntry.description: One entry of a conversation's input queue. The page it was submitted on is immutable: a queued command runs where it was typed.

steerEligible.description: Plain, attachment-free input in the eligible FIFO prefix may be absorbed at a tool barrier. A command or an attachment blocks everything behind it.

anyOf.description: JSON-RPC's null id, which a reply carries when the request it answers could not be read at all — a parse error or a frame that is JSON but not a request has no id to echo.

ResourceRevision.description: An expected revision carried by a mutation, so a stale write fails instead of overwriting a concurrently refreshed view.

ResponseResult.description: A successful reply's payload. Its shape is decided by the method that was called, and the frame does not repeat the method — so decoding takes one, exactly as a client holding its own request does.

RevisionScope.description: Which revisioned resource a precondition or change refers to.

RewindTarget.description: Where a rewind cuts back to.

oneOf.description: Back to the state before this item.
The most recent checkpoint, which is what `/rewind` with no argument means.
Everyone in the roster reads every post.
Posts reach the room's members when they next look.

userIsMember.description: The user joined, and may therefore speak.

RuntimeCollections.description: The unbounded collections a session owns, each as a revision plus the entries worth carrying inline.

ScopeId.description: A permission rule the server derived and would install for the session. Handed out with the prompt so `allowSession` names a scope the server verified rather than one the client composed.

ServerCapabilities.description: What this build can do, reported rather than inferred from model or provider names.

epoch.description: This process's run. Every resource ID belongs to it and dies with it.

oneOf.description: The client asked for it.
The transport reached EOF and the shutdown policy ran.
The session was replaced by a reset or a resume.

SessionId.description: The open session. Immutable within an epoch — a rename moves the storage locator and the display name, not this.

SessionListEntry.description: One persisted session as `session/list` reports it.

open.description: This session is the one currently open on this connection.

SessionLocator.description: How a persisted session is named on the wire. Opaque session IDs die with their epoch, so selection uses an explicit transcript locator instead.

oneOf.description: The most recently active session, which is what `/resume` with no argument and `--continue` both mean.
Exact transcript stem (`{slug}-{ts}`).
Exact transcript path.

SessionScope.description: A permission rule the server derived and verified, offered as the scope of an `allowSession` decision. Session-lived: never written to settings or the transcript.

SessionSnapshot.description: An atomic read of the session. Valid through `event_cursor`: the first event a client sees afterwards has a strictly greater `seq`.

SessionSummary.description: The session's own bounded state. Everything unbounded it owns is a collection.

resumed.description: The session resumed a persisted transcript rather than starting empty.

ShellDialect.description: Syntax family of the resolved shell, so a frontend can render (and a model can be told) what a command line will be parsed as.

ShutdownParams.description: EOF does the same thing. The shutdown policy interrupts active work and resolves interactions fail-closed before persistence and exit.

deniedInteractions.description: Interactions that were open and were resolved closed.

interruptedTurns.description: Work the shutdown interrupted on its way out.

Submission.description:
What a client submitted to a conversation.

`Composer` is the human path — leading slash, shell mode, and direct-address syntax all mean what they mean in the CLI, so a GUI cannot silently bypass them. `SendProse` is the explicit programmatic delivery that parses none of those forms.

SubmitDisposition.description: What the core did with a submission. The caller never chooses between these: queue-versus-steer, delivery-versus-turn, and command scope are the core's.

oneOf.description: Accepted behind a busy turn. Queueing never promises that steering will happen — if a tool barrier absorbs the entry, `queue/itemAbsorbed` says so.
Handed to a conversation that does not run a turn for it.
Parsed as an action and applied synchronously.

SuggestedAction.description: What would plausibly make it work. Advice, not a promise.

ThemeChoice.description: A persisted theme preference. Which colours a frontend actually paints is its own business; that this choice was saved is not.

ThinkingLevel.description: Thinking budget. `off` is a level rather than an absent value so a snapshot always answers the question.

Turn.description: One model or standalone shell run attached to a runnable conversation.

error.description: Why a failed turn failed. Present only with `status: failed`; the terminal event is still the turn's, not an error frame's.

inputItemIds.description: The completed items this turn consumed. They are ordered before `turn/started` and carry no `turnId` of their own.

round.description: Model requests inside the tool loop so far; a retry re-runs the same one.

TurnError.description: A turn's failure, in the same stable-code vocabulary as a request error.

TurnInterruptParams.description: Idempotent, and aimed at a server-issued turn ID: a late interrupt cannot cancel the next turn.

accepted.description: False when the turn had already reached its terminal state.

TurnOrigin.description: What started this turn. The console starts turns the user never typed — a mail digest wakes main on every frontend (`auto`).

oneOf.description: Prose the user submitted.
The next entry of the input queue draining.
A message from main or a peer that woke this conversation.
The core decided to run without an input of its own (mail digest wake).
A standalone shell run.

authoritative.description: This is the end-of-round accounting total rather than freshly streamed output: a rate sampler must not read the jump as a burst.
